chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

We were with him, and Ḥumrān was with him, when a mawla of his came in to him and said to him, “May I be made your ransom, this is ʿIkrimah in the throes of death.” He used to hold the view of the Khawārij, yet he was devoted to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. So Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to us, “Wait for me until I return to you.”

We said, “Yes.” Before long he returned and said, “Indeed, had I reached ʿIkrimah before the soul reached its place, I would have taught him words by which he would have benefited. But I reached him after the soul had already reached its place.”

So I said, “May I be made your ransom, and what are those words?” He said, “By Allah, it is what you are upon. So prompt your dying ones at the time of death with the testimony that there is no god but Allah and the wilayah.”

key_terms.النَّفْسُ: the soul; referring to the point at which life is departing
key_terms.الْخَوَارِجِ: the Khawārij; a sect mentioned to describe ʿIkrimah’s doctrinal leaning
key_terms.الْمَوْتِ: death; the final earthly moment being discussed in the narration
key_terms.الْوَلَايَةَ: the wilayah; allegiance and authority affirmed alongside tawhid
key_terms.شَهَادَةَ: the testimony; the declaration to be prompted at death
key_terms.كَلِمَاتٍ: words; the saving expressions Imam عليه السلام wished to teach

ai.seo_question: What should a dying person be prompted to say according to Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام emphasized the importance of prompting a dying person with the decisive words of faith before the soul reaches its final point. The narration identifies these saving words as the testimony of tawhid and the wilayah, highlighting their significance at the moment of death.
